title: Diwali 2026 in Singapore: Ten Indian Restaurants for Festive Feasts
excerpt: From a S$35 vegetarian feast at Nalan to Shikar's S$108 Sunday brunch, the Yahoo Lifestyle Singapore guide lists 10 restaurants, their Diwali dates and their mithai boxes.
body:
• Deepavali falls on 8 November 2026, with celebrations running from 6 to 10 November, according to the Yahoo Lifestyle Singapore guide syndicated by Seth Lui.
  • The guide lists 10 restaurants, from Shahi Maharani at Raffles City to Shikar at Maxwell Reserve, with set prices ranging from S$35+ at Nalan to S$108 for Shikar's Sunday brunch.
  • Several venues sell mithai gift boxes separately, including SanSara's 9-piece box at S$59++ and Rang Mahal's 12-piece collection at S$118+.
  • Book early: SanSara offers a 25% early-bird discount on mithai orders placed by 25 October, with collection until 8 November.

Singapore's Indian restaurants have published their Deepavali menus for 2026, offering diaspora families a choice that runs from a S$35 vegetarian feast to tasting menus above S$100. The festival, also known as Diwali, falls on 8 November this year, with celebrations from 6 to 10 November, according to the Yahoo Lifestyle Singapore guide. The list of 10 restaurants covers the city centre, Little India, Tanjong Pagar and the east coast.

The headline tables

Shahi Maharani, at Raffles City on North Bridge Road, leads the list with a Gastronomic Week built around a live Chaat Bazaar, regional curries including Rajasthani Laal Maas and Malabari Prawn Curry, and desserts such as Kulfi Pops, Rasmalai and Jalebis. Its weekday lunch buffet from 2 to 6 November is S$48++ for adults, the weekend lunch buffet from 7 to 9 November is S$58++, and the Grand Diwali Celebration Dinner on 8 November is S$88++ for adults. Its sweet boxes this year include a new Tropical Sunrise coconut-and-pineapple ladoo alongside Mango Surprise and Milk Cake.

SanSara, at the Grand Copthorne Waterfront Hotel on Havelock Road, runs its Diwali feast from 4 to 8 November. Both vegetarian and non-vegetarian set menus are S$88++, ending with Akhrot Halwa and ice cream. Shikar, at Maxwell Reserve on Cook Street, has no dedicated Diwali menu in the guide but offers a weekday lunch thali at S$65, tiered tasting menus from S$108 to S$168, a Sunday brunch at S$108, and a Diwali Mithai Collection at S$108. The guide notes Shikar serves beef, a detail worth checking for guests who avoid it.

Vegetarian, homely and regional options

AMRITH by The Song of India, on Race Course Road, serves a four-course Deepavali set from 6 to 10 November at S$68++ per person, for lunch and dinner, with vegetarian and non-vegetarian versions and refillable thali items. Its Legacy Collection 2026 mithai is available for collection and delivery from 1 October to 12 November. Nalan, at Capitol Singapore on Stamford Road, offers a 100% vegetarian Deepavali Royal Feast at S$35+, with vegan, Jain and no-onion-no-garlic options on request, and dishes including Kathal Dum Biryani and Makhana Kheer.

Vatan Se, on Tanjong Katong Road, takes a homely approach, with a Tandoori Platter, vegan Awadhi Galouti Kebabs, Daryaganj Butter Chicken and Lucknowi Dum Biryani, no service charge, and 10% off dine-in for guests who put their phones away. Sahebs, at Claymore Connect on Orchard Road, serves Punjabi dhaba-style food without a special Diwali menu; listed prices include Paani Puri at S$11, Pandara Road Butter Chicken at S$29 and Punjabi Rara Gosht at S$32.

Six traditions, live stations and modern fire cooking

The Manor by Awadh, at Amara Singapore in Tanjong Pagar, brings six Indian culinary traditions under one roof, with listed dishes from S$26 to S$46, including Chettinad Dum Biryani and Coastal Ghee Roast Prawns. Rang Mahal, at Naumi Hotel on Seah Street, runs a Diwali Thali Buffet from 3 November at S$58++ for lunch and S$68++ for dinner, with live street food stations. Revolver, on Tras Street, centres on open-fire cooking, with an Autumn Menu at S$89 in vegetarian and non-vegetarian versions; the guide notes Revolver also serves beef.

Mithai to take home

For gifting, the choices extend beyond the table. A separate Honeycombers guide lists Shahi Maharani's Celebration Box at $78+ for 15 mithai and its Royal Festive Box at $118+ for 24, with collection from 22 October to 9 November. The same guide lists modern mithai from Adda, from $48 a box, with flavours including masala chai barfi and salted caramel miso peda, available from 20 October. Rang Mahal's Mythical Garden Collection holds 12 pieces at S$118+, with 10% of net profits going to the Breast Cancer Foundation, according to the main guide. Revolver's limited-edition Diwali chocolate box holds 16 pieces at S$87.20.

What to do next

Diners should confirm current availability and prices directly with restaurants before travelling, as festive menus are limited to the dates listed above. Vegetarian families have the clearest value option at Nalan, groups seeking a buffet have Shahi Maharani and Rang Mahal, and buyers focused only on sweets can order mithai boxes without booking a table.
